falsifiers: The alleged physical sector has dimension at most three.
The recovery maps do not converge coherently, which instead fails the recovery gate.
cycles.next_obligation: Let inclusion degree p grow without bound.
cycles.question: Can the three-channel alpha=1,p=1 carrier ever establish observable density?
cycles.result: No, conditionally on coherent Hilbert-norm recovery and a physical sector of dimension greater than three. Its limit span is closed and has rank at most three.
cycles.title: Fixed-rank recovery obstruction
cycles.warrant: A span of at most three recovered limits is finite-dimensional and closed.

falsifiers: A(p) does not tend to zero.
For some fixed p, recovery error fails to vanish with cutoff removal.
cycles.next_obligation: Control Gram conditioning and all other errors on the same diagonal schedule.
cycles.question: Can fixed-p recovery estimates be assembled into one p(n) tending to infinity?
cycles.result: Yes conditionally. If approximation error A(p) tends to zero and recovery error R(p,n) tends to zero for each fixed p, a nondecreasing diagonal schedule p(n) can be chosen so A(p(n))+R(p(n),n) tends to zero.
cycles.title: Diagonal carrier-growth lemma
cycles.warrant: Choose N_p so R(p,n)<=1/p for n>=N_p, make N_p increasing, and set p(n) to the largest p with N_p<=n.

falsifiers: gamma_p collapses faster than Gram errors.
Whitening factors diverge and conceal vanishing raw OS norm.
cycles.next_obligation: Record raw eigenvalue intervals and couple p-growth to a conditioning budget.
cycles.question: When does increasing p preserve the intended OS quotient rather than amplify null directions?
cycles.result: For fixed p, rank is stable if the exact limiting Gram matrix has smallest retained eigenvalue gamma_p>0 and the matrix error is eventually below gamma_p/2. Along p(n), the ratio ||Delta G||/gamma_p must still tend to zero.
cycles.title: Gram-rank stability gate
cycles.warrant: Weyl eigenvalue bounds prevent a perturbation smaller than gamma_p/2 from crossing zero.

falsifiers: The target dictionary is not independently dense.
Residual convergence is only pointwise with no diagonal schedule.
cycles.next_obligation: Predeclare a countable Wilson-net target dictionary and its density theorem.
cycles.question: What does the Schur recovery residual actually prove?
cycles.result: Vanishing normalized residuals for every member of a separately dense target dictionary imply density of the carrier union in the dictionary closure. Residuals for two Wilson loops alone do not imply Hilbert-space density.
cycles.title: Recovery residual to density
cycles.warrant: The Schur complement is the squared OS distance to the carrier projection; density follows only after quantifying over a dense target family.

falsifiers: A computed trial value exceeds exp(-m*tau), refuting the proposed mass floor m.
Complement or leakage estimates remain uncontrolled.
cycles.next_obligation: Bound the complement transfer norm and carrier-complement coupling.
cycles.question: Can finite generalized eigenvalues certify the physical transfer gap?
cycles.result: Not alone. A trial carrier gives a lower bound on the full transfer Rayleigh supremum, so it can falsify a proposed upper bound. Gap promotion needs an upper bound including the carrier complement and off-diagonal leakage.
cycles.title: Visible Ritz bound polarity
cycles.warrant: A supremum over a subspace cannot exceed the supremum over the full physical sector.

falsifiers: No q_C<1 is available on the complement.
Leakage b does not vanish or remain below the reserved margin.
cycles.next_obligation: Produce a noncircular complement estimate; density alone at finite p is insufficient.
cycles.question: What finite-data inequality would suffice for a full transfer upper bound?
cycles.result: With physical-sector decomposition W plus W-perp, bounds q_W, q_C, and b on the two diagonal transfer blocks and off-diagonal block imply an operator upper bound given by the largest eigenvalue of [[q_W,b],[b,q_C]].
cycles.title: Transfer complement obstruction
cycles.warrant: The quadratic form is dominated by the corresponding two-by-two scalar majorant; its largest eigenvalue bounds the full contraction.

falsifiers: Positive-time matrices are mutually inconsistent.
The limiting translations lack strong continuity or the semigroup composition law.
cycles.next_obligation: Add multi-time correlation consistency and semigroup convergence to the recovery packet.
cycles.question: Does convergence of reflection-positive Gram matrices construct the continuum Hamiltonian?
cycles.result: No. Entrywise convergence of every recovered finite reflection matrix preserves OS nonnegativity, but Hamiltonian transfer also requires a consistent strongly continuous time-translation semigroup and convergence across physical times.
cycles.title: OS closed-cone versus semigroup convergence
cycles.warrant: Closedness of the PSD cone preserves positivity but supplies no semigroup law or generator convergence.

falsifiers: All centered recovered norms vanish.
The connected witness survives only after a proxy normalization or theory change.
cycles.next_obligation: Track norm survival and interaction witnesses as separate fields through the same trajectory.
cycles.question: Which witnesses prevent a vacuous or Gaussian limit?
cycles.result: A nonzero recovered OS norm prevents the carrier from vanishing. A surviving connected higher cumulant is a stronger non-Gaussian witness. Neither proves density, OS reconstruction, or a positive gap.
cycles.title: Nontriviality witness separation
cycles.warrant: These witnesses answer different logical questions and cannot substitute for one another.

falsifiers: Changing alpha also changes the action, normalization, or recovery convention.
Growing geometric radius fails to enlarge the OS carrier after quotienting.
cycles.next_obligation: Predeclare an alpha family and a separate degree-growth law p(n).
cycles.question: Which refinement variable can plausibly support density?
cycles.result: At alpha=1 in the candidate radius model, the number of lattice cells per shape stays bounded, making the pilot a UV-proxy falsifier. Values 0<alpha<1 permit growing shapes, but only explicit p-inclusion supplies the monotone density axis.
cycles.title: Geometric alpha versus algebraic p
cycles.warrant: Geometric scale and algebraic closure are independent controls and must not be conflated.

falsifiers: The required data cannot be produced without changing theory.
The mass floor collapses under p, volume, or cutoff refinement.
The recovered carrier is null, nondense, or limit-order dependent.
cycles.next_obligation: Produce the first actual alpha=1 Gram/recovery table and, independently, a quantitative p(n) error schedule; otherwise keep the route quarantined.
cycles.question: After ten bounded cycles, what remains viable and what is blocked?
cycles.result: Retain the two-axis alpha/p spectral-carrier route as a conditional research programme. The fixed-rank pilot is demoted to falsification. Proof promotion is blocked until actual same-theory SU(3) matrices, unbounded p-density, Gram stability, complement transfer control, OS semigroup convergence, and uniform cutoff/volume limits are supplied.
cycles.title: Consolidated YM route decision
cycles.warrant: Every finite or conceptual shortcut encountered has a named countermodel or missing transfer gate.
